## Updates

hown to the end user.

# Gathering calibration data

The next step of the calibration is to gather calibration data. In this
step, you basically tell the platform that you are about to go and gather
data from all the calibrating points on the given floor on the given
channel band and then perform it. The whole procedure is divided into
two stages, the first is to create a link with a map of calibration
points (steps 1-3) and the second is to perform the calibration at every
calibration point (steps 4-10). For the second stage, it is recommended
to read all the steps before performing the action.

Note

* The calibration should be conducted within the opening hours of the venue.
* Every time the venue or the access points change, calibration should
  be done again. To learn more, read the [Calibrating after editing a venue](recalibration.html) chapter.
* Before performing the calibration, it is useful to

again. To learn more, read the [Calibrating after editing a venue](recalibration.html) chapter.
* Before performing the calibration, it is useful to forget all other
  Wi-Fi connections so that your mobile device does not connect
  automatically to a different connection while calibrating.

To gather calibration data:

1. Go to **Location Management → Calibration**.
2. In the **Create link to calibration** panel:

   * From the **Venue** list, select the name of your venue.
   * Into the **Calibration device MAC address** field, type a MAC address of the device that you will use for calibration.
   * From the **Calibration name** list, select the name of your calibration.
   * From the **Floor** list, select the floor number on which you are going to perform the calibration.
   * Select the channel band at which you calibrate the access point (**2.4 GHz channel band** or **5 GHz channel band**).
   * **Only for advanced users**: If you want to allow adding new
     calibration points

   * **Only for advanced users**: If you want to allow adding new

# Get started with User Journey

## What is a User Journey and why is it important?

In general, a user journey is a map of steps which reflect users’ interaction with a product. It can be used in 2 ways: **to demonstrate** how the users are currently interacting with your product and **to design** their proper interaction with it.

### Why is it important?

When building a product or an interface, it is essential to create a friendly environment for the users. By friendly, we mean clear, not misleading and, most importantly, well-thought-out. For the more transparent it is, the more actively they will use it.

## Why should you create a User Journey for your users?

The User Journey feature allows you to design the way your users connect with your WiFi. It is **a graphic illustration of a login path**. You can arrange each step and decide what to display on your users’ scree

rs connect with your WiFi. It is **a graphic illustration of a login path**. You can arrange each step and decide what to display on your users’ screens. You can use it just for welcoming purposes but also for marketing ones.

Look at the example of a user journey created in our system.

![sample user journey](images/getting_started_with_user_journey/sample_user_journey.png)

**START** represents the moment a user connects to your WiFi. They are then redirected to the Portal which in this case is a login page. There, they fill in the **Form**. After clicking the **SUBMIT** button, they are given internet access for 1 hour. The Portal automatically redirects them to the Website of your choice, for instance to your company’s site.

It is but an example of what your users’ journey can look like. You can shape it freely according to your needs. For example, you can use the free space on the login page for marketing purposes, gather the data you need from a Form, or give your users access t

s. For example, you can use the free space on the login page for marketing purposes, gather the data you need from a Form, or give your users access to the Internet for a limited time. You can also use several Portals in the Page flow to extend the contact with end users and to expose them to more content. It’s all up to you.

## How can you use the User Journey in your business?

As already mentioned, you can use it to create a personalised login path, but there are other ways your business can profit from it.

### Monetisation

The Portal is the first level of contact with your users. On the login page, you can not only gather information about the users but also display other media, like advertisements or information about discounts. You can do the same with all of the other Portals which you have created in the Page flow. You can also resell the Portal’s free space to advertisers to display marketing content.

The adverts match the exact target group, so all parties benefit: end us

resell the Portal’s free space to advertisers to display marketing content.

The adverts match the exact target group, so all parties benefit: end users get what they are interested in, advertisers profit from returns on advertising, and your venue benefits from monetising your WiFi instead of only paying for it.

### Loyal customers

The adverts on the Portal will always match the end users. This will make them more eager to come back to your venue for more great offers. They may soon become your loyal customers.

# Page Flow Overview

As described in the User Journey Overview, a Page Flow (also called a Flow) is a graphic illustration of a login path which you can adjust according to your preferences.

Before you start building a Page Flow, prepare the initial idea of what your login path should look like in order to reflect it in the system.

## The Structure of a Page Flow

“START” represents the moment when a user connects to your WiFi. This is also when you start to build your users’ login path. Then, you design the login process and form the structure which will be displayed to users at each stage.

The windows that represent each step are called **nodes**. There are four types of nodes in the system: **Portal**, **Internet Access**, **Condition** and **Message**. You may access them by clicking the blue circle on the right side of a particular node:

![add nodes](../images/uj_page_flow_add_nodes.png)

Message**. You may access them by clicking the blue circle on the right side of a particular node:

![add nodes](../images/uj_page_flow_add_nodes.png)

By selecting **Portal**, you will be able to add a Portal to the Flow. You can select an already existing one or create a new one from scratch. Portals are used to gather user data through different methods of logging-in and various Forms.

**Internet access** gives users access to WiFi and enables them to set up network parameters. Since internet access is the main goal of the Flow, it is the core node in each login path. It can appear at different stages depending on how complex your user journey is.

**Condition** allows you to display personalised content to various user groups. For instance, based on the gender you may redirect your users to different Portals and send them advertisements aligned with their preferences.

* user profile data: age, gender

## Keep to Some Rules

There is no limit to the number of nodes in the Flow. However, there are some rules for creating it:

* Every login option creates a new exit from the node,
* The connection between the nodes must be ‘closed’ in order to finish the login path. This means that the node must be connected with another one (either an existing node or a new one),
* All nodes must be fully configured for the Page Flow to work correctly.

# Basic authentication

## Description

The authentication described here is required by some endpoints in order to give access to stored data. It is a standard implementation based on RFC7235 and RFC2617.

## Request

When you pass your credentials in the header, you must Base64-encode them in UTF8 and use the following format:   
`Authorization: Basic Base64(login:password)`

**Example:**  
`Authorization: Basic bXlMb2dpbjpteVBhc3N3b3Jk`

## Response

**Error responses**  
Code: 401 Unauthorized  
Description: The Authorization header or credentials are invalid.  
Header: `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm=Linkyfi`

Note

In most cases, the `realm` is **Linkyfi**, which means that you should use your Linkyfi credentials. Exact information about credentials are provided in specific endpoint section.

# POST / WiFiUserProfile

## Description

The **WiFiUserProfile** API is a push API that sends user data about users who successfully log in to WiFi or change
their data in the GDPR panel. It is sent every time a WiFi user gets access to the Internet, and/or makes changes to
their data.

It can be used to integrate the platform with services delivered by external providers, for instance, CRM software.

Push Method:  
**POST**

## Push URL

The **Push URL** is the URL of the server which receives the collected data.

* It must start with **https://**
* It is set in **Portal Management → Properties → Advanced properties**: the keys are *wiFiUserProfilePushApiUrl* and
  *wiFiUserProfilePushApiBasicAuthCredential*
  + *wiFiUserProfilePushApiUrl* sets the Push API
  + *wiFiUserProfilePushApiBasicAuthCredential* is **optional**, and when defined, it enables transferring user
    profiles to the URL with

Push API
  + *wiFiUserProfilePushApiBasicAuthCredential* is **optional**, and when defined, it enables transferring user
    profiles to the URL with Basic Authentication.   
    **Note: It must have a specific format: "login:password".**
* When a user logs in to WiFi or changes their data in the GDPR panel, the entire path is searched for the above
  properties: from the organisation in which they log in, to root. Then, the profiles are sent to the Push URL.
* It is recommended to use the properties in an organisation which acts as the Data Administrator

**Note:** If the notification option is **enabled** in the parent organisation, then, when a user logs in to the network
in a sub-organization, this sub-organisation will also trigger a notification.

# Requesting a Top-Up (for Clients)

If your Licence has used up all of its dedicated data transfer, you can request an additional top-up.

Such top-ups are derived from Data Transfer Packages which should be previously created by your Representative. So before you request a top-up, ensure they have them configured.

To request a top-up, go to the **Licence Manager**, and choose the desired Organisation. from the Organisation tree on the left.

1. In the top right corner of the desired Licence panel, click the **More** option and select **Request a Top-Up** from the dropdown menu.

ransfer Package** dropdown list. When you select a Package, you can preview its details below the dropdown list.

## Previewing Historical Requests

You can preview your requests and check their status by clicking the **Show Requests** button on the right side of the Licences workspace.

encoded message. This property is effective only for supported message types and is enabled by default (set on true).

# Creating, Editing and Removing an Organisation

To fully employ the platform's potential, you may want to reflect your company's structure in the system. This allows you to collect and analyse the data of all entities in your organisation. You can reflect your business' structure in the **Organisations** section by creating and accordingly arranging its members.

## Creating an Organisation

To be granted access to the platform, you should first receive the login credentials from the business partner responsible for setting up your account. Then, when you log in to the platform, your organisation should already be created there. Depending on the structure of your business, you may or may not need to create any sub-organisations. However, if your organisation has any subsidiaries which you would like to include in the structure, you can add t

ed to create any sub-organisations. However, if your organisation has any subsidiaries which you would like to include in the structure, you can add them as sub-organisations.

There is no limit to the number of organisations and sub-organisations which you may create.

## Adding a Sub-Organisation

1. Go to the **Portal Management → Structure** section and select **Organisations** from the navigation bar.

   **Before you begin creating a sub-organisation, make sure that you switched to the right organisation; it should be highlighted in blue.**
2. Now, click the **Add New Organisation** button to add a sub-organisation.

   ![adding organisation](images/organisations/create_suborg_1.png)
3. In the pop-up box:

   * Into the **Name** field, type the Organisation name (required),
   * From the **Time Zone** dropdown list, select the time zone in which your organisation is located (required),
   * In the **Platform Terms of Use** section, click the **Upload Document** button to upload t

zone in which your organisation is located (required),
   * In the **Platform Terms of Use** section, click the **Upload Document** button to upload the Terms of Use which platform users will be required to accept during their first login attempt (optional),
   * From the **Additional Settings** list, select the additional settings (optional, if applicable).
   * Then, click **Save** to confirm the changes.

   ![adding organisation](images/organisations/create_suborg_3.png)
4. A sub-organisation is now created.

   ![adding organisation](images/organisations/create_suborg_4.png)
5. To add another peer sub-organisation, repeat steps 1-4. **Before you proceed, make sure you switch to the desired level of organisation**.

## Switching the Organisation

You may switch the organisation, by clicking on the desired one in the right panel of the **Organisations** tab; such organisation should be highlighted in blue. You may also switch it on the platform top bar. To do this, click the **Organ

**Organisations** tab; such organisation should be highlighted in blue. You may also switch it on the platform top bar. To do this, click the **Organisation** dropdown list, and select the desired organisation. It should be highlighted in blue.

![switch organisation](images/organisations/switch_org_1.png)

![switch organisation](images/organisations/switch_org_2.png)

## Editing an Organisation

1. In the **List of Organisations**, select the organisation which you would like to edit. Then, click the **More** option on the right, and select **Edit**.

   ![edit organisation](images/organisations/edit_org_1.png)
2. Modify the Organisation details and click **Save** to confirm the changes.

## Deleting an Organisation

1. In the **List of Organisations**, select the organisation which you would like to delete. Then, click the **More** option on the right, and select **Remove**.

   ![remove organisation](images/organisations/remove_org_1.png)

ion on the right, and select **Remove**.

2. In the pop-up box, type the Organisation name into the **Enter the Organisation Name to Confirm** field to confirm deleting the Organisation. Then, click the **I Understand the Consequences, Remove Anyway** button.

### Release Date: 04/15/2021

## New Features

* We have implemented new columns to the **Sublicence Distribution** table in the Licence Package details window to provide you with even more complete reporting on the Package’s usage.
* We have also added new columns to the Sublicence **Top-Ups** table so that it provides you with more information on each top-up that has been made for a Sublicence.
* We have changed how data transfer requests are organised for Representatives. From now on, you can find all incoming requests in the **Pending** tab. Once you accept or reject one, it is then moved to the **Resolved** tab where you can display the history of all accepted and rejected requests.

# Creating Access Settings

The Access Settings feature represents your WiFi network and allows you to configure a WiFi network for your venue. You may set up the network’s name and connect it to the Page Flow.

With these settings, you may also create several networks at your venue; for instance, to distinguish a “public” network which should be used by your visitors from a “private” one, which should be used by your staff. You can do this by creating different Access Settings for each network. There is no limit to the number of networks which you may create.

he bottom right corner, click **+**.

# Managing User Roles

User Roles are sets of permissions which you can assign to Platform Users to determine their scope of Platform access.

## Creating a User Role

1. Go to the **Licences and Roles** section in the main menu, and select the **User Roles** tile. Then, click the **+** button in the bottom right corner.

   ![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_0.png)

   ![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_1.png)
2. In the first step of the User Role Creator:

   * Into the **Name** field, enter the name of the User Role
   * In the **Description** field, type the description of the Role (optional).

   Then, click **Next** in the top right corner to continue to the next step.

   ![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_2.png)
3. In the second step, determine Platform access by selecting the desired permissions from the dropdown sections.

   ![user roles](images/user_roles/user

n the second step, determine Platform access by selecting the desired permissions from the dropdown sections.

   ![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_3.png)

   ![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_4.png)
4. In the last step, you can review the User Role setup and preview the set of permissions by clicking the **Show List** button.

   To finish creating the Role, click **Save** in the top right corner.

   ![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_5.png)

## Editing a User Role

To modify a User Role’s scope of access, click the **More** option on the preferred User Role, and select **Edit** from the dropdown list.

Then, follow the steps from the **Creating a User Role** sub-chapter, and make the desired changes.

![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_15.png)

## Deleting a User Role

To delete a User Role, click the **More** option on the preferred User Role, and select **Delete** from the dropdown list.

![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_16.png)

If the

**More** option on the preferred User Role, and select **Delete** from the dropdown list.

![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_16.png)

If the User Role is assigned to Platform Users, in a popup-box, you can select another Role which will be assigned to them, or select the **Do Not Assign Another Role** option.

Note

Selecting the **Do Not Assign Another Role** option will leave the assigned Users with **no Platform access**.

![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_19.png)

## Previewing the User Role Usage

You can see the number of Platform Users assigned to a Role by checking the **Number of Assigned Users** label in the User Role’s panel. You can also preview the full list of assigned Users.

1. To preview the User Role usage, click the **More** option on the preferred User Role, and select **Preview Usage** from the dropdown list.

   ![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_17.png)
2. In the new window, you can see the list of Platform Users assigned to this Role. T

own list.

   ![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_17.png)
2. In the new window, you can see the list of Platform Users assigned to this Role. To go back, click the **<** icon in the top left corner.

   ![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_18.png)

## Previewing Permissions

User Role panels allow you to preview the full list of permissions selected for Roles.

To do this, click the **More** option on the desired Role panel, and select **Preview Permissions** from the dropdown list. Then, in the next window, you can see the full list of permissions selected for that Role.

![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_6.png)

![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_7.png)

## Comparing User Roles

You can compare sets of permissions selected for two different User Roles.

1. Choose a Role which you would like to compare with, and click the **More** option on its panel. Then, select **Compare Roles** from the dropdown list.

   ![user roles](images/user_roles/user_roles_13.

and click the **More** option on its panel. Then, select **Compare Roles** from the dropdown list.

# User Journey Overview

User Journey is a platform feature which allows you **to create a personalised login path to your Wi-Fi**. To access it, go to the **User Enrollment → User Journey** section

![user enrollment user journey](images/uj_access.png)

In this section, you can see four components with which you will design a personalised user login path. These are: **Page Flow**, **Portal**, **Access Settings**, **Form**, and **Loyalty Programs**. Each of them has their own editors.

## Page Flow

A Page Flow (also called a Flow) is **a graphic illustration of a login path**. As was previously mentioned, you may shape it according to your needs.

The Flow can be very simple, with one Portal (a login page) and Internet Access. Or, it can be very complex as well. See the images below.

![sample user journey](images/uj_page_flow_sample.png)
Picture 1: A Simple Page Flow

![sample user journey 2](image

x as well. See the images below.

![sample user journey](images/uj_page_flow_sample.png)
Picture 1: A Simple Page Flow

![sample user journey 2](images/uj_page_flow_complex.png)
Picture 2: A Complex Page Flow

## Portals

Portals are the pages which are displayed to users. They have a variety of uses in the login path. The Portal, which plays a key role in the Flow is the **login page**, where the users gain internet access. The Portals, however, may also be used to authenticate users, display marketing content, or communicate with WiFi users.

To learn how to create and edit a Portal, go to the **Portals** chapter.

## Access Settings

The Access Settings feature is your network manager. Essentially, it is the most important part of the User Journey because it makes the Page Flow visible to the users. It allows you to configure a network which you will provide to your venue. You may create it, give it a name which will be displayed on the users’ devices with other WiFi networks, and t

which you will provide to your venue. You may create it, give it a name which will be displayed on the users’ devices with other WiFi networks, and then **connect the Page Flow to it**.

To find detailed instructions on how to manage the Access Settings, read the [Creating Access Settings](create_access_settings.html) chapter.

## Forms

Forms are questionnaires which you can use on the Portals. They are not required in the User Journey process, but are a great tool to gather user data. For instance, you may use a Form on your login page and collect gender, age, and email information from those users who log into your WiFi. You can also create custom survey questions according to your needs. Creating a Form is similar to creating a Portal.

To learn how to create and edit a Form, go to the **Forms** chapter.

## Loyalty Programs

Loyalty Programs enable you to launch marketing campaigns that allow users to collect stamps and receive token codes which they can redeem for rewards. It is

Programs enable you to launch marketing campaigns that allow users to collect stamps and receive token codes which they can redeem for rewards. It is a useful strategy to encourage users to shop or use your services regularly.

### To start building a Page Flow, read the [Page Flow Overview](page_flow/page_flow_overview.html).

# Platform overview

## What can you do with the platform?

1. Manage Wi-Fi networks in your organisations
2. Create a Wi-Fi login process (User journey)
3. Gather Wi-Fi statistics
4. Promote your business
5. Gather data about customer venue behaviour
6. Create navigation around venues

## How does it work?

### Where can you start?

You simply [reflect the structure](reflect_the_structure_of_your_business.html) of your organisation in the platform, [create a user journey](/guide/use_cases/user_journey.html), and [statistics](wifi_statistics.html) are being gathered automatically.

You can also [promote your business](promote_your_business.html) with various marketing actions.

Additionally, with the location function of the platform, you can [create navigation around venues](creating_navigation_for_customers.html) which customers can open in their web browsers and at the same time provide yo

reate navigation around venues](creating_navigation_for_customers.html) which customers can open in their web browsers and at the same time provide you with [behavioural data](/guide/use_cases/understanding_the_behaviour_data.html). It doesn't mean you have to create the navigation to gather such data, it's just a great way to invite more customers to log in to Wi-Fi.

### Propagation of settings

Settings are propagated down the organisation tree. The structure of organisations in the platform is represented in a form of a management tree, such as in the image below.

![organisation tree](images/management_tree.png)

With the propagation, you don't need to implement particular settings in every organisation.  
It is enough to implement them in an organisation which is on a higher level in the tree, and they are automatically propagated to all organisations on lower levels.

Also, numerous editors in the platform have panels divided into two sections: **Own** and **Inherited**. Element

o all organisations on lower levels.

An example of such panel is the **Page Flow manager**.

# Troubleshooting

The **Troubleshooting** section allows you to track all the configuration issues between Access Points and Page Flows in
your Organisation. To access it, go to the **User Enrollment** section in the left menu, and select **Troubleshooting**
from the dropdown list.

![troubleshooting](images/troubleshooting.png)

In the **Configuration Issues** table you can find details of issues which occur in your Organisation and
Sub-Organisation:

* the **Date** column shows the date an issue occurred,
* the **Issue Type** column informs about the type of this issue,
* the **Count** column displays the number of problems that need resolving,
* the **Device ID** column provides the ID of the Device in which the issue has occurred,
* the **Organisation** column displays the Organisation which is impacted by the issue,
* the **Request Information** column provides you with the detailed information on

** column displays the Organisation which is impacted by the issue,
* the **Request Information** column provides you with the detailed information on the Access Point (AP Name) and
  Network (SSID Name) in which the issue has occurred.

## Configuration Issues

The most common configuration issues that you might encounter include **AP not found**, **SSID not found**, **SSID and
AP not found**, **Flow not attached to Network**, **Licence error encountered**, **Social config not found**, and
**Login loop encountered**.

### AP not found

The message `AP not found` highlights issues related to the AP (Access Point). It could indicate that the AP name in the
Platform is misspelled or incorrect, the AP has not been added to the Platform, or has been added but to an incorrect
Organisation.

To resolve this issue, you should verify the AP setup in both the AP and the Platform, ensuring accuracy on both ends.

### SSID not found

The message `SSID not found` indicates issues related to the Ne

in both the AP and the Platform, ensuring accuracy on both ends.

### SSID not found

The message `SSID not found` indicates issues related to the Network (SSID). This could mean that the specified Network
cannot be found on the Platform, has not been added to it, or differs from the Network configured on the AP (Access
Point).

To resolve this issue, you should examine the Network setup in both the AP and the Platform, ensuring accuracy on both
ends.

### SSID and AP not found

The message `SSID and AP not found` points to issues with both the AP (Access Point) and the Network (SSID), combining
the two scenarios mentioned above.

To resolve this issue, you should inspect the Network and AP setups in both the AP and the Platform, ensuring their
accuracy across all aspects.

### Flow not attached to Network

The message `Flow not attached to Network` indicates that no Page Flow has been connected to the specified Network
(SSID).

To resolve this issue, you should link the desired Page

to Network` indicates that no Page Flow has been connected to the specified Network
(SSID).

To resolve this issue, you should link the desired Page Flow to this Network.

### Licence error encountered

The message `Licence error encountered` indicates that processing could not be performed due to a licensing error within
the Organisation.

To resolve this issue, you should ensure that the Organisation has a proper and valid Licence set up on the Platform.

### Social config not found

The message `Social config not found` indicates that processing could not be performed due to the absence of a Social
Media login configuration.

To resolve this issue, you should ensure that the Organisation either has a primary Social Media configuration selected,
or the Captive Portal used in the Page Flow utilises a custom selected Social Media configuration. Please note that this
issue may occur with various types of social media.

### Login loop encountered

The message `Login loop encountered` in

ration. Please note that this
issue may occur with various types of social media.

### Login loop encountered

The message `Login loop encountered` indicates that processing was halted due to the detection of a login loop. This
typically suggests that either the RADIUS is incorrectly set up, or it is being blocked by some firewalls.

To resolve this issue, you should ensure that the proper RADIUS configuration is applied on AP (Access Point) and that
the Platform's RADIUS server is reachable from the AP. Additionally, verify that there are no firewalls blocking UDP
communication on ports 1812 and 1813.

# Location API

The **Location API** enables the identification of user location. You can find the Location API endpoints listed below.

To view the additional Location API, go to the [API Documentation](/API), and see the **Historical Location** section.

## GET /location/{venueId}/allLocations

It returns information on all users and their position at the venue which can be displayed in the Device Mapper. The user location is determined in relation to the point (0,0) specified in the Venue configuration.

### Request

Authentication: *Basic Auth*  
Method: *GET*  
URL: */location/{venueId}/allLocations*

URL parameters:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| venueId | string | ID of the Venue visible in Portal Management / Structure / Venues |

### Responses

#### Success response

Code: *200*

#### Description

Format: JSON object

Response elements:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | ---

## Responses

#### Success response

Code: *200*

#### Description

Format: JSON object

Response elements:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| locations | object | keys: macs of devices, values: corresponding positions of devices |

Position element:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| x | string | User's location against x axis |
| y | string | User's position against the y axis |
| floor | integer | Floor number where Device is located |

#### Example

```
{
 "12:34:56:78:FF:AA": {
   "x": "-37.9",
   "y": "46.5",
   "floor": 1
 },
 "10:30:47:61:12:AF": {
   "x": "-150.5",
   "y": "28.7",
   "floor": 1
 }
}


```

#### Error responses

Code: *404 Not found*

Description: *The provided venueId in the URL parameters does not exist*

We have introduced the long-awaited update to the **Licences** feature which is now visually consistent with the rest of the Platform. We have also reviewed and redesigned the licencing mechanism, so it’s more user-friendly and allows you to manage your Licences more efficiently.

The new **Licences** allow you to create **Licence Packages** which contain Access Points that can be further distributed among your clients as **Sublicences**. It also provides a smart overview of your Licences with a quick view on AP capacity and time left for them to expire.

You can also set up email notifications on Licences, such as expiry, removal, or updates, and manage their sending details.

To learn how to manage Licences, go to the **User Guide > Licences and Roles** section.

# Unify Network Controller Configuration Guide (v7.4 or above)

## Prerequisites

To configure Unifi V7.4 and above access point controllers with the platform, you should fulfill specific prerequisites and prepare the basic configuration.

## The Configuration Prerequisites

* For Unifi V7.4 and above make sure to prepare the following:
* Check the version of Unifi Controller. It must be version 7.4 or the latest version.
* Make sure that **https://<controller\_domain>:<port>** or **http://<controller\_ip>:<port>** of the controller is in Public and able to reach Platform’s corresponding cloud server.
* Prepare a user credential with “Site Administrator” role in Unifi. Please take note of Username and Password.

w are connections measured?*

# Release Version: 21.09.17\_\_stable\_\_0.51.0

### Release Date: 09/17/2021

## New Features

* We have added a new and **important security feature**, the ability to set up and configure a **Time-Based One Time Password Two-Factor Authentication** when logging in to the platform. From now on, during logging into this feature can be either **recommended**, **required** or **turned off**. An additional option has been implemented, **Remember me**, which allows the user not to enter the token code every time if using the same device. The **Two-Factor Authentication** set-up view is available for the user until the correct code is entered for the first time. The view becomes available again when the user **secret key** is reset in **Portal Management > Structure > User section**. The option of configuring the **Two-Factor Authentication**for an organisation is possible o

eset in **Portal Management > Structure > User section**. The option of configuring the **Two-Factor Authentication**for an organisation is possible only by our administration.

* In the **Device Mapper** in **Dashboard > Behaviour**, the activation of the **Panic Button** changes the device’s color to a **warning color**.

* In the **Users Now** table of the **Dashboard** we have changed the list of all **user organisations** and the list of all their **devices** to the current device used to log in and the organisation they last logged into.

**Note:** Earlier data can be found in **Raw Data > WiFi Users** table.

* When creating and editing a **Payment Plan** in the **network parameters** step, the option to set the total data transfer has been added.

# Creating calibration points

Now that you created the calibration you can place the calibration points on your venue plan.

Best practices regarding the placement of calibration points

The placement of calibration points is important for the calibration accuracy and the scanning time.   
The distance between calibration points should be **from 3 to 5 metres** (8 metres distance is also sometimes permissible, but it is not recommended).  
Here are some additional basic requirements for the placement of the calibration points:

* In large rooms, they should be placed in the corners and beside walls.
* In small rooms, one calibration point may be enough; otherwise, they should be placed only in the corners.
* In narrow passageways, they should be placed along the passageway.
* In wide passageways, they should be placed along the passageway, on both its sides.
* Characteristic obj

they should be placed along the passageway.
* In wide passageways, they should be placed along the passageway, on both its sides.
* Characteristic objects (for example: poles, stands, partition walls) should have additional calibration points placed next to them.

For more details, read **Indoor Location – Best Practices Guide**

To create calibration points:

1. In the **Calibration** panel, click ![add calibration point](images/image156.png) and place the markers of the calibration points on the plan.

   Tip

   Use the **Hide/Show grid** button to, respectively, hide the measuring grid or show it.

   ![add calibration point](images/image164.png)
2. To stop adding calibration points, next to the icon, click **Close**.

**What to do next**: [Configure access points](configuring_access_points.html)

The Location Statistics consist of three tabs which you can find at the top of the statistics window: the **Overview**, the **Rush Hour**, and the **User Behaviour**. ### Visible

The **Visible** table displays the number of unique users who have been situated within your WiFi network's reach. Their devices must have been spotted by access points at least once within the designated period, but their location *may or may not be known*.

### Located

The **Located** table shows the number of unique users who are situated within the network's reach. They differ from the Visible Users by their location, which *is known*.

### Visible and Located Users

![location stats](../images/location_statistics/location_statistics_3.png)

The **Visible and Located Users** bar chart presents the total number of Visible and Located Users. These data are displayed as a total number, broken by these two types. It may be shown per hour, day, and week.

![location stats](../images/location_statistics/lo

![location stats](../images/location_statistics/location_statistics_4.png)

The **Min. and Max. End-User Count** bar chart shows the minimum and maximum number of all user types.

### Ratio Located / Visible

The **Ratio Located / Visible** chart displays the ratio of the number of users located and visible, calculated in %.

## Rush Hours

![location stats](../images/location_statistics/location_statistics_5.png)

The **Rush Hours** section provides the graph which presents the distribution of hours when the user traffic is at a peak. It is a heat map which displays the average number of users per hour, in colours; the higher the number of Logged-In Users, the darker the shade of the given field is. It is a visualisation of daytime traffic at your venue, which allows you to identify the time of day when the user congestion is at its peak, and adequately

a visualisation of daytime traffic at your venue, which allows you to identify the time of day when the user congestion is at its peak, and adequately plan the customer service deployment.

To view the number of users at a specific time, hover your mouse over the appropriate area.

## User Behaviour

### New and Returning Located Users

![location stats](../images/location_statistics/location_statistics_6.png)

The **New and Returning Located Users** bar chart shows the total number of new and returning located users. It may be presented per hour, day, and week. To view the exact number, hover your mouse over the desired bar.

You can also filter this graph by the type of users. To do this, select the preferred user type from the legend located in the top right corner of the table.

![location stats](../images/location_statistics/location_statistics_7.png)

### Dwell Time Distribution of Located Users

The **Dwell Time Distribution of Located Users** bar chart displays the distribution

### Dwell Time Distribution of Located Users

The **Dwell Time Distribution of Located Users** bar chart displays the distribution of the number of sessions by their duration.

### Average Dwell Time for Located Users

The **Average Dwell Time for Located Users** doughnut chart presents the average duration of all user sessions. It is calculated for Located Users as a total duration of all sessions divided by the total number of sessions.

sues, though our platform was not vulnerable to them.

The multi-step login process differs from other login processes in that it is created from two paired components:

**Phone Number Input** and **Phone Number Verification** is used for two-step phone number verification,
**Pay to Access** and **Payment Method** is used for paid access.

Both components must be reflected in Portals and the Page Flow. You must first create two Portals and then place them in the Page Flow in their proper order.

**You should note that in order to use the Pay to Access method, you must first have a valid PayPal account which should be connected to the platform.**

ting a Portal](creating_portal.html) chapter.

# Previewing End-User Devices

When you have correctly configured your Venue in the **Location** mode, you can preview the real-time position of end-user devices on Venue maps.

The **Device Mapper** table displays Visitors' position at your Venue live.

You should ensure that the Ruckus ZoneDirector controller:

- Is given access to the platform via ports *80*, *1812* and *1813*,
- Is connected and communicating with Access Points,

You should also make certain that:
- The Ruckus ZoneDirector firmware version is **9.13.1** (9.10 for https redirection).
- You are logged in to the Ruckus ZoneDirector web interface.

# POST / Accounting Session

## Description

The **Accounting Session API** is a push API that sends accounting session data to an external server on every session
start and end.

It can be used to integrate the platform with services delivered by external providers.

Push Method:  
**POST**

## Push URL

The **Push URL** is the URL of the server which receives the collected data.

* It must start with **https://**
* It is set in **Portal Management → Properties → Advanced properties**: the keys are *sessionPushApiUrl* and
  *sessionPushApiBasicAuthCredential*
  + *sessionPushApiUrl* sets the Push API
  + *sessionPushApiBasicAuthCredential* is **optional**, and when defined, it enables transferring sessions to the URL
    with Basic Authentication.   
    **Note: It must have a specific format: "login:password".**
* When a session starts or ends, the entire path is searched for the above
  propertie

**Note: It must have a specific format: "login:password".**
* When a session starts or ends, the entire path is searched for the above
  properties: from the organisation in which they log in, to root. Then, the profiles are sent to the Push URL.
* It is recommended to use the properties in an organisation which acts as the Data Administrator
* Property *sessionPushApiCustomerRefPropertyName* is optional and stores name of dynamic property storing value of
  customerRef to be sent along with session data

## Message

Format: JSON object  
Message elements:

| Name | Format | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `emailData` | EmailData / null | Email data |
| `createdTime` | Long | Timestamp in milliseconds |
| `updatedTime` | Long | Timestamp in milliseconds |
| `customerRef` | String / null | Customer Ref |
| `bytesDown` | Long | Bytes downloaded |
| `bytesUp` | Long | Bytes uploaded |
| `sessionDuration` | Long | Duration of the session in seconds |
| `eventType` | String | start

s downloaded |
| `bytesUp` | Long | Bytes uploaded |
| `sessionDuration` | Long | Duration of the session in seconds |
| `eventType` | String | start / stop |
| `deviceID` | String | Device ID |

### EmailData

| Name | Format | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `emailAddress` | String | Email address |
| `confirmationDate` | Long / null | Timestamp in milliseconds. When null, it means the email is not confirmed |

  "bytesDown": 1000,

## Prerequisites and Basic Configuration

To configure the Ruckus vSZ Access Point with the platform, you should first fulfill specific prerequisites, and prepare the Basic Configuration.

### Configuration Prerequisites

You should ensure that the Ruckus controller:
- Has correctly configured IP settings, and is connected with the DNS server,
- Can resolve the domain address which is ***domain**.com*,
- Is given access to the platform via ports: *80*, *1812* and *1813*,
- Is connected and communicating with Access Points.

You should also make certain that:
- The end device has been given access to the port **9997** of the management plane, cluster plane of vSZ, or in case of Ruckus GRE tunnel - an external IP,
- The firewall for the http and https re-directions should have ports **8090** and **8099** **opened**.

The **Loyalty Programs** feature enables you to launch marketing campaigns that allow users to collect stamps and receive token codes which they can redeem for rewards. It is a useful strategy to encourage users to shop or use your services regularly.

1. Go to the **User Enrollment > User Journey** section, and select the **Loyalty Programs** tile.

   ![loyalty programs](../images/loyalty_programs/loyalty_programs_1.png)
2. In the **Loyalty Programs Manager**, click the **+** button located at the bottom right corner to create a new Loyalty Program.

   ![loyalty programs](../images/loyalty_programs/loyalty_programs_2.png)
3. Firstly, type the name of the Program in the **Name** field. Then, click **Next** in the top right corner to proceed to the next step.

t** in the top right corner to proceed to the next step.

   ![loyalty programs](../images/loyalty_programs/loyalty_programs_3.png)
4. In the following step, determine the terms of the Program:

   * Select the number of stamps that users must collect to receive rewards by moving the **Number of Stamps** slider right or left
   * To set the minimum time which must pass before obtaining another stamp, turn the **Min. Time Between Stamp Collection** switch **ON**, and specify the period in the input and dropdown fields
   * To determine how much time users have to collect all the stamps, turn the **Max. Stamps Collection Period** switch **ON**, and define the period in the input and dropdown fields
   * To determine how much time users have to redeem their token codes for rewards, select the **Token Validity Upon Receipt** switch **ON**, and specify the period in the input and dropdown fields
   * From the **Number of Token Codes** toggle button, select how many times users can redeem th

# Find your way around Wi-Fi Users statistics

## About Wi-Fi Users statistics

The Wi-Fi Users statistics panel provides combined footfall data for a selected time frame and is located in **Reporting → Statistics**.

At the top of the panel, you can select the time frame for which you want to see the data. By default, it shows the last seven days.

![date picker](images/stats_calendar.png)

The whole panel is divided into four sections:

* **What do you know about Users' visits?**
* **Which suborganisation do the data come from?**
* **Who are the Users?**
* **What do you know about Connections?**

## Definitions

Throughout the Statistics following terms are used:

**User** - a person who logged in to Wi-Fi,  
**New user** - a User who:

* logged in to Wi-Fi for the first time ever,
* didn’t log in within the preset interval,
* in any type of gran

o Wi-Fi,  
**New user** - a User who:

* logged in to Wi-Fi for the first time ever,
* didn’t log in within the preset interval,
* in any type of granularity (hourly, daily, yearly) can be recognized as new and returning at the same time.

  Example

  If a User logs in for the first time one day, even though seen as returning in daily granularity (because of the second login), he is defined as new user for the purpose of statistics.

**Returning user** - a User who is not new and logged in to Wi-Fi within the preset interval,
**Connection** - a connection to a Wi-Fi network,  
**Device** - every device that can connect to Wi-Fi, such as: a mobile phone, a computer, or a smart device. It is identified by a Device ID (usually it is a MAC address of a device).

Tags serve as data points for platform users and are replaced by the system with specific values. For instance, the *$firstName* tag serves as a data point for a user's first name. It is replaced in the final content (SMS, Email) with the user's first name. If the tag cannot find a proper value, it displays a default value which was previously set up in the system.

The full list of tags is in **Tag Settings** where you can configure the tags according to your preferences.

# Release Version: 21.05.13\_\_stable\_\_0.42.0

### Release Date: 05/13/2021

## New Features

* We have integrated yet another type of device with the Platform - the **D-Link** access point.

## Updates

### System Updates

* We have modified the way Token codes are generated so that they do not contain characters that may be hard to distinguish, such as `I`, `l`, `1`, or `o`, `O` and `0`.
* In Organisation Subtree Manager, we have blocked transferring Organisations that use Loyalty Programs or Payment Plans, which will not be available after the Organisation has been moved.
* We have enabled the CoA Disconnect Message support for the Ubiquiti devices.
* We have also added the CoA port customisation for devices that already support CoA requests.

## Resolved Issues

### GUI Fixes

* The autofill function in captive portals would work incorrectly and make it difficult

ady support CoA requests.

## Resolved Issues

### GUI Fixes

* The autofill function in captive portals would work incorrectly and make it difficult for users to log in to WiFi. We have fixed it, and it should not disturb user flow anymore.
* We have also fixed incorrect highlighting of modified Licences.

### System Fixes

* On captive portals, when the user skipped a form that contained a dropdown list, they would receive an error page. We fixed it and forms now work correctly.
* The user's internet connection could not get automatically renewed after they were prematurely disconnected from an access point if a downgrade from `HTTPS` to `HTTP` was needed to communicate with the device. We have improved how flows are processed so that downgrading does not affect the end user.
* User Accounts with no data limits would get disconnected from the WiFi as if they exceeded their data limit, even if data limiting was disabled for the whole Organisation. This has occurred in Organisations wi

om the WiFi as if they exceeded their data limit, even if data limiting was disabled for the whole Organisation. This has occurred in Organisations with configured CoA for devices and should no longer happen.
* For username types of User Accounts with defined contact email addresses which have not been stored in `WiFiUserProfile`, password reset would fail to work. We have fixed it, and it should now work smoothly.

# What’s New in November 2020

## Brand-New Adding Venues

We have reviewed and updated the process of adding Venues to the Platform, which is now visually consistent with the rest of the Platform interface.

We have also moved it to the **Portal Management > Structure** section; it is now located in the Structure upper bar to facilitate managing Venues in Organisations.

**Note:** To use the **Venues** feature, you must first have your Organisation set to the **Location** mode.

![add venue](images/11/creating_venue_1.png)

## New Timeout Option

We have introduced the new type of **Timeout** in the Page Flow nodes - **Hour** - that allows you to specify the exact hour of the day, after which the user’s sess

uced the new type of **Timeout** in the Page Flow nodes - **Hour** - that allows you to specify the exact hour of the day, after which the user’s session would reset.

### How It Works

#### Use Case

A user is given internet access for one hour per day. Until now, Flow nodes allowed you to configure the session reset only to a specified interval, such as 24 hours. So, if the user browsed the internet on November 1, from 7 to 8 PM, then on the following day, November 2, they would have to wait until 7 PM to gain internet access again. But what if they would like to use it earlier?

#### Solution

The **Hour** option enables you to designate an exact hour of the day when internet access resets. You can set up the reset hour to a preferred one, such as midnight or any other, which would allow the user to browse the internet any time on November 2.

To do this, click the **More** option on the desired node, and select **Timeout** from the dropdown menu. Then, in the pop-up box, select **H

mber 2.

To do this, click the **More** option on the desired node, and select **Timeout** from the dropdown menu. Then, in the pop-up box, select **Hour** from the available options, and specify the time in the selector. To confirm your changes, click **Save** in the bottom right corner of the popup-box.

![timeout](images/11/timeout_hour_1.png)

![timeout](images/11/timeout_hour_2.png)

## Data Transfer Limits

We have implemented the new mechanism which controls data transfer used by WiFi users and terminates user sessions when they reach determined limits.

In the process, we have updated the transfer counting per user which now, apart of counting transfers per sessions, is based on the `UserAccountingEvent` events. Data transfers will also be checked when users log in to the network; if it is used up, users will not be able to log in to your WiFi.w

**Note:** To limit data transfers, you should enable the `userAccountTransferLimitsEnabled` property for the desired Organisations by

to your WiFi.w

**Note:** To limit data transfers, you should enable the `userAccountTransferLimitsEnabled` property for the desired Organisations by changing its status to `true`.

You can preview data transfers for all user accounts in the **List of User Accounts** table in the **Access Methods > User Accounts** section.

To ensure that data limits are working correctly, we recommend using devices which support transfer limits and configure them accordingly. Devices supported by the Platform include: CISCO, Ruckus controller, Meraki, Ruckus SZ/vSZ/vSCG, Ruckus SCG 3.2-3.4, RUCKUS\_VSCG\_CLOUD, and other.

For more configuration details, see the **Device Configurations** chapter in the User Guide.

## Managing a Portal Node

You preview the specific Portal Node. click the **More** option on the desired Portal Node, and select **Preview** from the menu.

In the next window, you can select the preferred settings (the language and the display mode, if applicable) to see the Portal. To go back to the Page Flow, click the **Close Preview** option in the top right corner.

![preview portal node](../images/page_flows/preview_portal_node_1.png)

### Setting Up a Portal’s Timeout

Portal Nodes allow you to set up the **Timeout** which is a designated period after which, when no action undertaken, the user is redirected to the beginning of the login path. This

p the **Timeout** which is a designated period after which, when no action undertaken, the user is redirected to the beginning of the login path. This option is particularly useful in Flows which contain more than one Portal.

To set it up, click the **More** option on the desired Portal Node, and select **Timeout** from the menu. It is especially useful in Flows with more than one Portal.

![portal node timeout](../images/page_flows/portal_timeout_0.png)

Now, in the pop-up box, select one of three options which determine the timeout of the Portal:

* The **Time** option determines time after which the user is redirected to the beginning of the login path,
* The **Number** option allows you to designate the number of times the specific Portal is displayed to the user before redirecting them to the beginning of the login path,
* The **Unlimited** option enables unlimited access to the Portal, and the user is not redirected to the beginning of the login path.

When you have finished des

imited** option enables unlimited access to the Portal, and the user is not redirected to the beginning of the login path.

![portal node timeout](../images/page_flows/portal_timeout_1.png)

### Editing a Portal Node

You can edit a Portal directly from the Page Flow, however, such Portal can be edited only to some extent (for instance, submit buttons cannot be edited in this mode). You should also note that **the changes applied to such Portal are visible in all Page Flows which use this Portal.**

To learn more about editing Portals, read the [Editing, Copying and Deleting a Portal](../portal/copying_portal.html) chapter.

![editing portal node](../images/page_flows/edit_portal_node.png)

To remove a Portal Node from the Page Flow, click the **More** option on the desired Portal Node and select **Delete Node** from the menu.

ove a Portal Node from the Page Flow, click the **More** option on the desired Portal Node and select **Delete Node** from the menu.

The **average display time** should be **less than 5 min**, and **should not exceed 10 min**. In case it is higher, try reloading the page, or change the date range. If the data is still not displayed, contact your administrator.

To ensure the best system performance, part of the data is stored in probabilistic structures, therefore the expected error in relation to real data can be up to 0.1%.

In most cases, the statistic calculations are based on **Logged-In Users**, which means users who have com

n relation to real data can be up to 0.1%.

In most cases, the statistic calculations are based on **Logged-In Users**, which means users who have completed the login process and gained internet access. In other cases, the user type is indicated.

To view these statistics, go to the **Reporting > Statistics** section and select **Engagement** from the upper bar. They can be displayed for a specified time frame; to define it, select the time range in the **Time Picker** located at the top of the Statistics panel, and click **Show** to confirm your selection.

# Managing a Licence

A **Licence** is a set of Licences which you can assign to your Client. They can only be derived from Licence Packages. So to create a Licence, you must first have a Licence Package assigned to you for distribution.

To learn how to create a Licence Package, read the [Managing a Licence Package](licence_package.html) chapter.

## Creating a Licence

1. Go to the **Licences and Roles** section in the main menu and select the **Licence Manager** tile.

   ![sublicence](images/licences/licence_package_0.png)
2. First, you should ensure to have switched the current Organisation to the Sub-Organisation for which you would like to derive a Licence, or create a new Sub-Organisation.

   To switch the Organisations, select the desired Sub-Organisation from the Organisation tree on the right. To learn how to create a new Sub-Organisation, read the [Creating, Editing and Removing an Or

# Marketing Campaigns Overview

Marketing Campaigns allow you to reach your users with special offers via text messages (SMS) and/or emails that may encourage them to return to your venue. On the platform, you can find five types of Marketing Campaigns: **One-Shot**, **Recurring**, **Birthday**, **Time-Limited**, and **Location-Based**. They differ by the dispatch schedule, which means the campaign sending frequency.

## Campaign Types

### One-Shot Campaign

The **One-Shot** campaign can be used to dispatch a one-time offer to your users.

### Recurring Campaign

The **Recurring** campaign can be used to send users an offer several times in a designated time frame.

### Birthday Campaign

The **Birthday** campaign can be used to send a special offer to a user on their birthday.

**Note: For this kind of campaign to work correctly, the data on the date of birth must be collecte

send a special offer to a user on their birthday.

**Note: For this kind of campaign to work correctly, the data on the date of birth must be collected during the login process. This may require configuring appropriate login option which gather such data.**

### Time-Limited Campaign

The **Time-Limited** campaign can be dispatched only in a designated time frame. It is sent to all the users that are already in the selected target group, and is continually sent to new users who fall into the targeted audience.

### Location Campaign

Due to configuration differences, the **Location-Based** campaign is described in a separate chapter. To learn more about it, read the [Creating and Managing a Location-Based Campaign](location_based.html) chapter.

## Campaign Editor

All campaigns have dedicated editors which consist of seven steps:

* The **Campaign Overview** step where you can enter the Campaign Name and the Campaign Description,
* The **Target Group** step where you can determine the

**Campaign Overview** step where you can enter the Campaign Name and the Campaign Description,
* The **Target Group** step where you can determine the audience to which you would like to direct the campaign, by creating a desired target group. There is no limit to the number of groups which you can create,

  Note: You may be required to create a Marketing Category which the users should accept during the login process. To learn how to create it, read the [Creating and Managing a Location-Based Campaign](location_based.html) chapter.
* The **Marketing Categories** step where you can select marketing categories by which the recipients should be targeted,

  Note: You may be required to create a Marketing Category which the users should accept during the login process. To learn how to create it, read the [Creating and Managing a Location-Based Campaign](location_based.html) chapter.
* The **Contact Method** step where you can determine how you would like to contact your users: via text m

sed Campaign](location_based.html) chapter.
* The **Contact Method** step where you can determine how you would like to contact your users: via text message (SMS), email, or both,
* The **Message** step where you can design the content of the message, and send a test message to the designated phone number,
* The **Delivery Schedule** step where you can configure the dispatch schedule (it can be configured in advance),
* The **Summary** step where you can preview the summary of the campaign before saving it.

# Configuring access points

Before gathering calibration data all access points need to be
specifically configured for that process. Perform the configuration according to
the appropriate manual. In case when there is no manual for your device, perform
the following procedure.

Warning

Without this step data gathered by the calibration will be incorrect and will significantly worsen the accuracy of the location.

To configure the device:

1. For both channel bands, 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz, set all access points to
   work on the same single Wi-Fi channel.

   Note

   Due to the country-specific radio regulations, working on all access points on a particular Wi-Fi channel can be impossible, even if explicitly set. For example, in the countries regulated by the FCC, due to weather radar systems avoidance regulations, for the channel band 5 GHz, it can be impossible to have all access poin

ies regulated by the FCC, due to weather radar systems avoidance regulations, for the channel band 5 GHz, it can be impossible to have all access points working on single channel 100 and above.
2. Create two independent SSIDs/networks: one for the channel band 2.4
   GHz and the second for the channel band 5 GHz. Calibration of each
   point must be performed for both channel bands consecutively using a
   device connected to the SSID dedicated to the specific channel band.

**What to do next**: [Gather calibration data](gathering_data.html)

# Checking activity stream

Activity stream enables you to check what changes were applied in the
platform, who applied them and when.

To check an activity stream:

1. Go to **Portal Management → Activity stream**.
2. Select a filter. You can choose:

   * **User login** – shows changes applied by a user.
   * **Organisation** – shows changes applied within an organisation.
   * **Single entity** – shows changes applied in a selected type of actions, such as captive portal edition.
   * **Entity group** – shows changes applied in a group of actions, such as organisation’s structure edition.
3. From the calendars, select a **Start date** and an **End date**.
4. Into the **Search for phrase** field, type a searched phrase.
5. Click **Show**. As a result, you can see all the
   changes applied.
